spec.classification: ETF transfer and signal feasibility; not faithful replication or independent confirmation
stages: SPY next-open execution with net-order costs
spec.variance: prior full calendar-month daily excess-return variance, ddof0; RF from author archived daily data; exact date alignment required
spec.normalization: c = sd(monthly SPY excess)/sd(monthly SPY excess/lagged variance) on calibration only, frozen thereafter
spec.signal: monthly SPY weight min(1,c/prior-month variance), no shorting or leverage; no parameter sweep
spec.execution: previous month close signal, first exchange session open to next month first open; synthetic adjusted units; net-order fees self financed; final liquidation
spec.cash: compound archived daily RF from entry-session date through session preceding exit; realized cash accrual approximation, not a decision feature; monthly-close diagnostic uses matching monthly compounded RF
spec.controls: same-execution full SPY and fixed calibration-volatility-matched SPY allocation (ratio of capped-strategy/calibration-market standard deviations, capped at 1). No realized test-period risk matching.
spec.primary: net monthly alpha on same-execution market excess return; positive risk-adjusted usefulness requires base alpha>=1 pp/year, positive lower95 bound and Holm p<=.05 at all predeclared block lengths; positive alpha at 2x/4x costs
spec.secondary: return, drawdown, turnover/cost, exposure and return versus calibration risk control; not alternative success gates
spec.inference: 5000 synchronized stationary bootstrap paths, block lengths 6/12/24 months, seed24001, refit alpha each path; Holm across 3 cost scenarios. Conditional on frozen calibration c. Diagnostic bridge alphas not additional discovery claims.
spec.precision_rule: If any base adjusted p in [.04,.06], increase all block runs to 20000; decision still requires all blocks. Report Monte Carlo SE.
limitations: Daily RF and adjusted units approximate actual cash/dividend accounting
This is a monthly signal, not a demonstrated several-day effect
